summary: Park ticket after N post_run_verify reopen failures

delivery.outcome: Bound the post_run_verify reopen loop. PostRunVerifyConfig gains max_reopens (default 3, 0 disables). apply_verify_failure counts prior post_run_verify-failed notes via planfile ticket show --format json (new count_verify_failure_notes helper); once the ticket reaches the budget, on_failure=reopen escalates to a terminal blocked status (action parked) instead of another open, which the queue would redrive. This stops the observed PLF-2599-style drive->verify-fail->reopen->redrive loop that burned 49 drive cycles.
nonGoals: Changing queue post_run_verify semantics for on_failure=block
Altering shell_drive_finalize behavior or capability detection
Changing drive retry limits in cycle_drive_retry or decision_arbiter
Marking the ticket done inside the verifier

architecture.decision: Parking reuses the existing planfile blocked terminal status and the same update --status command shape as reopen, so no new planfile capability is required. The reopen budget is durable evidence: it counts notes already persisted on the ticket rather than volatile in-memory streaks, so restarts do not reset it. Unknown note shapes degrade to reopen (fail-open to legacy) while unreadable ticket JSON yields None and also falls back to reopen.
architecture.rollback: Revert the ticket commit; legacy unbounded reopen restored, or set max_reopens: 0 in koru.yaml.

validation.evidence: 89 passed; new tests cover parked-after-budget, boundary (2<3 reopens), max_reopens=0 legacy, and note-shape counting. Persistence call-sequence tests unchanged and green.
